PullRequest.Title: Use SDK-owned Copilot marketplace installation records

Related to #343342. This is an independently useful marketplace-installation prerequisite, not a complete fix for that issue.

## Summary

Replace `AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider`'s dependency on `IAgentPluginService.plugins` and `copilotCliInstallation` with SDK-owned installation records.

- Add a typed `IAgentPluginInstallation` / `listPluginInstallations` seam through the provider, agent service, local management IPC, and local host service.
- Use Copilot SDK 1.0.25 global `plugins.list` as installation authority. Keep disabled installations and live marketplace records; exclude built-ins and managed desired entries explicitly reported as not installed. Do not promote session-effective/client-provided plugins to installation ownership.
- Project SDK records into `IRecordedCustomizationMarketplaceResource`, including direct-source disambiguation for uninstall, verified provenance, versions, descriptions, and icons.
- Complete install/uninstall on the SDK transaction instead of waiting up to 30 seconds for the removed client discovery inventory. Refresh through the existing provider change event.
- Preserve selected backend session/chat routing for mutations and inventory requests, and reject remote sessions at the local-only bridge rather than reading this machine's inventory.
- Preserve retained catalog associations for unique verified name/repository/revision matches; leave ambiguous matches unassociated.
- Cover marketplace installed-state/resource association with no client plugin discovery and no invented installed filesystem URI.

This does not remove `CopilotCliAgentPluginDiscovery`, change genuinely client-provided plugin publication, or include the parent's local-customization forwarding changes. Hooks/MCP discovery publication remains separate work in #343572. No generated protocol files or SDK APIs were changed.

## SDK limitations

Global `plugins.list` supplies durable plugin identities and verified repository/revision metadata. Session `plugins.list` is effective runtime state, can contain non-installed/session-only plugins, and does not supply the same verified metadata, so it is not merged into installation ownership.

The SDK list does not expose cached plugin paths or verified plugin roots. `installedFrom` is a live marketplace directory, not an installed plugin path. This change deliberately does not infer private cache layouts, synthesize a filesystem URI, or reconstruct missing roots. Exact URI-based joins to a separately discovered plugin remain unavailable without upstream metadata. Retained catalog associations remain in-memory, and ambiguous same-name/repository/revision installations cannot be associated with a particular catalog root.

The inventory seam follows the existing local-only marketplace management bridge. This does not add a new remote wire-protocol management capability; remote sessions cannot accidentally consume local installation records.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto current `main`, using Node 24.22.0.

- **Passed**: client output build.

  ```sh
  npm run build-fast -- --client-only
  ```

- **Passed: 86 tests** covering the marketplace provider and install-service suites, SDK inventory filtering, service forwarding, and existing live-session mutation routing.

  ```sh
  ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --grep 'AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider|CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService|lists persisted SDK plugin installations|installs and uninstalls plugins through the owning provider|prefers a live session for plugin marketplace operations|uninstalls plugins through the SDK server API'
  ```

- **Passed**: client TypeScript check.

  ```sh
  npm run typecheck-client
  ```

- **Passed**: changed-TypeScript ESLint, without warnings.

  ```sh
  npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostManagementService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotFailureTelemetry.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts
  ```

- **Passed**: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`.
- **Passed**: commit pre-commit hygiene hooks; commit is GPG-signed with the configured key.

Initial dependency bootstrap (`npm run install-fast`) encountered extension-registry authentication `E401`; no credentials or registry configuration were changed. Available root dependencies supported all successful checks above. Live authenticated SDK installation flows, remote-provider installation management, and full integration/smoke suites were not exercised.

## Manual verification

1. Select a local Copilot Agent Host session and browse a configured marketplace.
2. Install a plugin, then verify that the catalog reports it installed and the operation completes without waiting for client plugin discovery.
3. Uninstall the recorded plugin and verify the catalog returns to available.
4. For same-name direct installations, verify uninstall targets the selected SDK direct-source identity.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added await, complete call path to client.rpc.plugins.list(), broad event sources, and absence of request cancellation/coalescing are explicit in code. Exact event burst size and SDK list duration vary by session, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SDK subprocess RPC calls and serialized plugin inventory objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For E session customization updates (including MCP server state transitions and subscription snapshots), this adds E global plugins.list RPCs; because refreshProviderInstallations only increments a version and does not cancel or coalesce prior work, a burst can leave up to E reads in flight concurrently.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess IPC/subprocess work and delayed marketplace installed-state refreshes, with CPU/serialization pressure during MCP state-update bursts.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: getPluginInstallations synchronously read the already-published IAgentPluginService observable, so customization-driven provider refreshes did not cross the SDK plugins.list boundary before loading receipt inventory.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every getInstallations refresh now awaits getPluginInstallations, which crosses the renderer/agent-host bridge and calls client.rpc.plugins.list(), before it starts the existing listCustomizationInstallations request.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 290 changes the plugin portion of every provider refresh from a synchronous local observable read to an awaited host/SDK inventory request, placing one new plugins.list boundary call on each broad customization-update path.
Findings.Title: Coalesce plugin inventory reads across customization updates
Findings.Impact: After the customization install service has been activated for a Copilot session, each SessionMcpServerStateChanged/session subscription update triggers another provider refresh. Rapid MCP startup/authentication transitions therefore issue overlapping global plugin inventory RPCs, and the latest installed-state update also waits for this new RPC before the existing receipt inventory request can begin.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.onDidChange includes agentHostCustomizationService.onDidChangeCustomizations; WorkbenchAgentHostCustomizationService fires that event for SessionMcpServerStateChanged and every subscribed session-state change. CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService responds by calling refreshProviderInstallations, whose refreshVersion rejects stale responses but neither cancels nor reuses their requests. The changed await at line 290 reaches CopilotAgent.listPluginInstallations -> _retryAfterClosedConnection -> client.rpc.plugins.list(), then only afterward invokes listCustomizationInstallations.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache/coalesce the global plugin inventory independently of broad customization state events (invalidate it on host start and plugin mutations, with a bounded refresh path for external changes), and share any in-flight read. Also start the independent plugin and receipt inventory requests together so the plugin RPC does not add a serial round trip to the installed-state critical path.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: After the SDK install transaction completed, the operation remained on the critical path waiting for the separately published client plugin-discovery observable; waitForPluginInventory bounded that unrelated synchronization at 30 seconds.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Plugin install/uninstall actions could remain pending for up to 30 seconds when client discovery did not promptly publish the SDK mutation, as encoded by the removed pending-until-inventory tests.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed install/uninstall paths complete after the authoritative SDK mutation and fire the existing provider refresh event instead of awaiting client discovery.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Deleted LEFT line 359 removes await this.waitForPluginInventory(..., true, token) after install; the same wait is removed from the second install and uninstall paths, and the deleted helper raced the observable against pluginInventoryUpdateTimeoutMs = 30_000. The replacement test verifies mutations complete through SDK records without waiting for client discovery. Blame attributes the old critical-path wait to the supplied introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and refresh marketplace installed state for the active local Copilot Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService binds the provider or receives provider.onDidChange, calls getInstallations, and cannot publish the authoritative provider snapshot until the new plugin inventory read completes and the existing receipt inventory read subsequently completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly introduced call per provider refresh event, with no grouping or in-flight reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Plugin records were read synchronously from IAgentPluginService.plugins, so this boundary did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the existing receipt inventory request is started and before installed state can settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Global Copilot SDK client.rpc.plugins.list RPC and response serialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per renderer inventory refresh; E events produce E calls and can overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No global SDK plugin-list RPC was made by provider refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one serial SDK round trip before receipt inventory and consumes subprocess/serialization work for stale refresh generations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing receipt inventory management call, internally listing skill/MCP/config records
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per refresh; internally the SDK performs three grouped parallel reads, plus bounded recovery on recovery-required results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the only host inventory phase after the synchronous local plugin read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already required, but the diff starts it only after the new plugins.list call, adding serial latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number E of customization/session-state events, including MCP server startup/authentication transitions; plugin count P controls response serialization and projection, while pending catalog associations are bounded at 1000.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each event starts a refresh immediately. refreshVersion discards stale responses but does not cancel/coalesce their work, so up to E plugin inventory reads can overlap during an event burst; SDK client startup is coalesced, but plugins.list calls are not.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Plugin installation inventory has no positive, negative, or in-flight cache: cold and warm refreshes both call plugins.list. Session receipt inventory is cached only as an error fallback and still performs its authoritative read on each refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event sources, lack of cancellation/coalescing, sequential await placement, and the SDK RPC call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact MCP event burst size, SDK RPC duration, and installed plugin count vary by session; this lowers severity but does not affect the proven uncoalesced one-call-per-event mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the diff adds an uncoalesced global SDK RPC to every broad customization refresh and serializes it ahead of existing receipt inventory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a configured or marketplace Copilot plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user action awaits the existing installPlugin management/SDK transaction, then returns after firing provider change; the ensuing inventory refresh is asynchronous and off the mutation promise's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing installPlugin management call followed by SDK plugins.install
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK mutation ran, then the caller additionally waited for client discovery inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains the authoritative mutation critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one after the provider event, plus any concurrent customization events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconciliation consumed the locally published plugin observable instead of invoking global plugins.list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the install promise critical path but required for installed-state UI reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One SDK install transaction per distinct resource operation; the post-change refresh count follows emitted provider/customization events rather than plugin collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The install service deduplicates a pending operation by resource key. The post-install refresh participates in the uncoalesced event behavior described above.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No plugin inventory cache is used after mutation; the refresh rereads global SDK installations. Existing receipt fallback caching is unrelated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted waits and replacement event-driven refresh are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK install duration is environment-dependent, but the removed discovery wait was explicitly bounded at 30 seconds.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the mutation latency improves materially by removing the up-to-30-second client-discovery wait; the post-event inventory fan-out is covered by the reported refresh finding.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed path first lists global plugin installations to verify a unique current identity, then invokes the existing SDK uninstall transaction; it no longer waits for client discovery afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: New management and SDK plugins.list identity validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per uninstall attempt, regardless of warm provider inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identity was resolved synchronously from the client plugin observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one serial read before the uninstall transaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mutation ran and was followed by an up-to-30-second discovery wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One from the provider event, plus broad customization events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: UI reconciliation used the local plugin observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the uninstall promise critical path and used to reconcile UI state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One full plugin list scan and one uninstall RPC per user action; filtering is linear in installed plugin count P. The ensuing provider refresh performs another list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single action is serialized by awaits; same-resource uninstall operations are tracked by the install service. Provider refresh work can overlap with other customization events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retained identity/inventory cache is reused for uninstall, so warm actions still relist; catalog association state is bounded to 1000 entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the list-then-uninstall sequence and deleted wait are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The one pre-uninstall list round trip may be small on a warm client; the removed discovery wait dominates worst-case latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the current-identity validation is bounded to one user action and the PR removes a substantially worse wait; repeated refresh cost is covered by the reported event-scaled issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request installation inventory for a remote Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getBackendSession rejects a non-ambient connection authority before invoking the local listPluginInstallations bridge.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected session; no plugin collection is read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No boundary work is launched after rejection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted or populated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: authority check precedes the host call and is covered by a changed test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance because the local boundary is not reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: remote sessions do not accidentally trigger local SDK inventory work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium-confidence-high finding for uncoalesced plugins.list RPCs on broad customization events, and recorded the PR's removal of the prior 30-second post-mutation discovery wait as a concrete regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
